text:
incident-bot: Paging oncall: PROD GPU pool 'prod-gpu-1' at 95% util, queue length 1,230, avg queue wait 8.2s, error spike 4.3%. Trigger=autoscaler_failed (rate-limit). Severity: P1. @mia (oncall)

mia (oncall): ack — investigating, grabbing dashboard + autoscaler logs. putting pager into focus.

alex (eng-runtime): +1 seeing lots of CUDA Xid 31 and repeated kernel OOMs in node logs, nodes flapping in last 10m. suspecting driver runtime instability reducing effective capacity.

aurora (sre): linking recent deploy? any rollout touching drivers?

alex (eng-runtime): no recent driver rollout. But here's repeated pattern from dmesg across nodes: ```[ 12345.678901] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31, pid=23456, GPU=0, Channel='Gfx'```
followed by: ```kernel: Out of memory: Killed process 23456 (python) total-vm:12000000kB```. multiple nodes  gpu-11/gpu-12/gpu-15.

mia (oncall): queue growth + autoscaler not scaling because of rate-limit on scale requests. customers hitting throttles. need immediate mitigation: fallback routing, cordon flapping nodes, kill noisy jobs.

jay (infra): looking at autoscaler logs — it's hitting cloud provider API quota: "InstanceQuotaExceeded: max-instances 50 in region-us-west". Current desired was 58, provider rejected. autoscaler is marking as failed and backing off.

aurora (sre): oncall plan: 1) divert traffic away from prod-gpu-1 to prod-gpu-2 fallback pool (lower-capacity, quantized models) 2) cordon & drain most-flapping nodes 3) escalate to infra for temporary quota bump 4) restart drivers on nodes showing Xid 31 5) customer comms. I'll start routing change now.

liz (cust-success): I'm getting inbound from two enterprise customers about timeouts for embedding endpoints — they report 504s. Can we get ETA for recovery? I'll prepare an interim status.

mia (oncall): aurora, please switch routing. alex, can your team prepare a graceful restart procedure we can run node-by-node? we need to avoid mass pod evictions causing more queue backlog.

aurora (sre): routing change applied: `router set-weight prod-gpu-1=0.25 prod-gpu-2=0.75` and enabled prefix-caching for embed endpoints. Observability: queue dropping to 760 but still high.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy rollback: model-serving v12 -> v11 triggered by aurora at 1968001280.

alex (eng-runtime): procedure: 1) cordon node, 2) drain with `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`, 3) restart driver: `sudo systemctl restart nvidia-driver && sudo dmesg -T | tail -n 50` 4) check for Xid in `dmesg` and GPU health with `nvidia-smi -q`. doing this on gpu-12 first.

mia (oncall): do it one node at a time, confirm queue impact before next.

alex (eng-runtime): restarting driver on gpu-12 now. logs: ```Restarting nvidia-driver... OK
[ 12346.000000] NVRM: GPU 0000:65:00: GPU is now online
[ 12346.500000] INFO: nvidia-smi reports no ECC errors``` No Xid seen after restart (first 2m).

aurora (sre): cordoned gpu-15 (most flappy), drained, moved 120 pods off. Noticed several pods in crashloop due to OOM. Marking those workloads for quota review.

jay (infra): requested quota bump to 70 instances with cloud provider support (case #CLOUD-9941) and opened priority support chat. Also temporarily enabled burst capacity in policy to allow 8 extra instances pending approval.

mia (oncall): good. any change in customer impact?

liz (cust-success): still seeing some 504s but rate dropped. I've sent a short status to affected customers: "we are mitigating GPU capacity issue; partial traffic moved to fallback pools; working on driver restarts and scale requests; ETA 30-60m"

aurora (sre): queue now 220 and avg wait 2.1s. error rate down to 0.7%. autoscaler showing successful scale-to-58 now (post-burst policy), pending actual instance allocation.

alex (eng-runtime): restarted drivers on gpu-11/gpu-12/gpu-15. gpu-11 had persistent Xid 31 before restart and had kernel OOMs tied to a user process doing large batch inferences. we've added resource limits to the deployment causing the OOM.

mia (oncall): added temporary rate limit on large-batch route to 30qps to protect pool while we observe.

jay (infra): cloud provider increased quota to 65 while support approves higher. Instances provisioning now in progress, should be backfilled in ~12m.

aurora (sre): also enabled autoscaler backoff override for this incident (manual) to prevent backing off on transient API errors.

liz (cust-success): sending updated note: "Progress: traffic partially diverted; driver restarts complete on flapping nodes; provisioning additional capacity; monitoring. Next update in 30m."

mia (oncall): summary of mitigations applied: routing diversion, driver restarts on 3 nodes, cordon/drain of flapping nodes, temporary burst capacity enabled, rate-limit on heavy route, resource limit added to offending deployment. Monitoring queue & errors.

aurora (sre): recommend post-incident: 1) root cause analysis of why driver started OOMing — investigate memory spikes in model worker, 2) enforce pod resource requests/limits for large-batch jobs, 3) tune autoscaler to surface quota rejections to oncall earlier and optionally fallback to alternate regions, 4) add alert for sustained Xid 31 rate.

mia (oncall): leaving handoff to next oncall in 20m, will follow up on RCA. For now incident is mitigated, not resolved.

alex (eng-runtime): will collect dmesg, nvidia-smi history and OOM kill traces and start a ticket.

liz (cust-success): queued customer follow-up templates in #customer-updates, will send once we have final restoration. :thumbsup:

aurora (sre): closing out immediate pager, marking incident as mitigated. creating postmortem stub and linking logs to internal ticket.

mia (oncall): thanks all. switching channel to incident-review in 30m.
